events.text: Your first visit to the Isle Bazaar, you hold out a handful of Low-Grade stones for a cloud-lotus, and the stallholder laughs: up here, nobody counts Low stones one at a time.

effects.log: You laugh. They sell you the lotus at a fair price, and teach you to count by weight.
You pay. You learn later what it should have cost.

events.text: A trader at the Exchange weighs your stones on a jade scale and says three of them are hollow: old fakes from the world below.

ok.log: The scale is the fake. The trader goes red.

effects.log: You accept it. The trader is very polite for the rest of the day.

events.text: The Exchange posts its rate at dawn: today a Mid-Grade stone buys eleven Low, not twelve, because a faction is buying Mid stones quietly for a war.

effects.log: You sell. By evening the rate is back. You made a little.

ok.log: A clerk tells you. You know something the isles do not.

fail.log: The clerk is very interested in why you ask.

effects.log: You do nothing. The war never comes. You sleep well.

events.text: A stallholder looks at your plain robe, sees no faction badge, and quietly doubles the price chalked on the board.

effects.log: You pay. Being nobody's is expensive above the clouds.
They shrug and rub the chalk out. "Mistake," they say.
The next stall is no better, but it is honest about it.

events.text: An usher at the Lantern Auction looks at your name, your faction (none), your standing at the Court, and seats you behind a pillar.

effects.log: You bid blind and win something odd. It turns out to be good.

ok.log: You are moved, grudgingly, to the second row.

effects.log: You leave. The pillar was the best seat for listening anyway.

events.text: At the Lantern Auction an heir of the Eight Houses bids against you for a lot you want, and keeps raising by exactly one stone.

effects.log: You win, at a price that hurts. The heir bows, amused.
You stop. The heir looks disappointed: they wanted the game.
You jump the bid. The heir laughs and lets it go.

events.text: In the Under-Cloud Market below the isles, a demon with a lantern offers to sell you a pill that will make your next breakthrough easier, or kill you.

effects.log: You buy it. You never use it. Knowing you could is enough.
You refuse. The demon shrugs and sells it to the next immortal.
The wardens come. The stall is gone before they arrive.

events.text: Someone at the Isle Bazaar lifts the stone-pouch from your sleeve so lightly you only notice when you go to pay.

ok.log: You catch a child of the isles, who gives it back and asks how you knew.

fail.log: They are gone into the crowd, and so is the pouch.

effects.log: You let it go. Somebody needed it more, or less.

events.text: It is stipend day at the Jade Court, and the line of immortals waiting for their stones stretches across three bridges. You are near the end.

effects.log: You wait. You hear every rumour in the Upper Realm.

choices.text: Give your place to an old immortal

effects.log: You give it up. They never forget it.
You push forward. People remember that too.

events.text: A rumour runs through the Exchange: a vein of High-Grade stones has opened on a drifting isle, and nobody has claimed it yet.

ok.log: It is real, and small, and you fill your sleeves.

fail.log: It is a rumour. The isle is empty, and windy.

effects.log: You sell it to three traders before noon.
You ignore it. By evening it is a different rumour.

events.text: A stallholder offers you a relic of the first immortal to climb the white stairs. They have, by your count, sold nine of them this year.

effects.log: You buy it. It is a very good fake.
You tell them. The stall closes. Nobody thanks you.
You walk on, smiling.

events.text: At the Cloud Crane Roost a crane chooses you, walking out of the flock and standing on your foot until you notice it.

effects.log: The keeper says a crane that chooses is not for sale. It follows you anyway, for a while.
You put it back. It looks at you as if you were very slow.

events.text: You owe a trader of the Lantern Guild a few stones, and the trader has begun sending cranes with reminders, each one politer and more alarming.

effects.log: You pay. The cranes stop.
You work a season at the trader's counter. The debt is paid and you learn the trade.

events.text: A drifter with no faction sits by the Exchange gate with an empty bowl. Immortals walk past as if the drifter were weather.

effects.log: You fill it. The drifter nods, as one rogue to another.
You sit with them. You learn more about the Exchange than in a year inside it.

events.text: Two stalls at the Isle Bazaar are in a price war over spirit herbs, and the herbs are cheaper than they have been in a thousand years.

effects.log: You buy a season's worth.

choices.text: Warn the stallholders they will both go under

effects.log: They stop, grudgingly. The herbs go back up.

events.text: A minister offers to keep your stones in the Jade Court's own vault, safe from thieves, for a small yearly fee and the right to lend them out.

effects.log: You agree. Your stones are safe, and working for someone else.
You refuse. You keep them in your sleeve, like a drifter.

events.text: A Mid-Grade stone in your pouch cracks in your hand, and its qi rushes out into the air of the Exchange. Everyone nearby breathes deeper.

effects.log: You breathe it in. A little energy, gone in a moment.

choices.text: Let it go to the crowd

effects.log: The crowd smiles without knowing why.

events.text: A teller of fortunes at the Isle Bazaar reads stones instead of palms, and asks for one of yours to read.

effects.log: The teller reads it and says you will be rich in something other than stones.
The teller reads your refusal instead, and says the same thing.

events.text: Your first visit to the Divine Exchange, you learn that faith is not counted but felt, and that the stallholders can feel exactly how much you have.

effects.log: They feel it and are polite. A small god is a customer like any other.

ok.log: You hide it well. They treat you as an elder god, briefly.

fail.log: They feel you hiding it, and laugh.

events.text: At the Star Market a measure of luck you are about to buy is being weighed on scales that tilt toward the seller.

effects.log: The seller swaps them, embarrassed.
You buy it. Luck is luck.

events.text: The Divine Exchange posts what a prayer is worth this age. A pantheon has been buying faith quietly, and the price has risen.

effects.log: You sell. The price falls back by the next age.

ok.log: A clerk tells you. You know something the sky does not.

fail.log: The clerk asks why you want to know.

effects.log: You hold. Nothing happens. It is restful.

events.text: A stallholder of the Divine Exchange sees that you stand in no pantheon, and asks a quarter more faith for everything.

effects.log: You pay. It is the price of walking alone.

choices.text: Name the stall's own pantheon's rules

effects.log: They go quiet and charge the right price.

events.text: At the Star Market's auction a lot comes up that nobody bids on: a single dried prayer from a world that no longer exists.

effects.log: You buy it for almost nothing. Sometimes, at night, it whispers.
It is thrown away. You think about it afterwards.

events.text: A god of an Elder Lineage bids against you at the Star Market for a lot you want, raising by a single prayer each time.

effects.log: You win, dearly. The elder god is amused.
You stop. They look disappointed.

events.text: At the Market Beyond the Twelve, past the edge of every pantheon's domain, a god with no name sells you the dream of a sleeping god.

effects.log: You buy it. You dream it once, and know a secret.
You refuse. The god with no name shrugs.
The Court sends clerks. The market moves.

events.text: Someone at the Divine Exchange has siphoned faith from you so quietly you only notice the cold where it was.

ok.log: You follow it to a starving small god. You let them keep it.

effects.log: You let it go.

events.text: It is tithe day for your pantheon, and gods queue at its hall to give faith and be seen giving it.

effects.log: You give generously and are seen.
You give what is owed. Nobody notices.

choices.text: Give quietly to a smaller hall

effects.log: You give to a small god's hall instead.

events.text: A rumour runs through the Divine Exchange: a new world has been born at the edge of the sky, and has not yet chosen what to pray to.

effects.log: You go. A few of its first prayers are yours.
You leave it. It will choose well, or not.
You sell it to three pantheons.

events.text: A stall offers the first prayer ever spoken, sealed in amber. You have seen seven of them today.

effects.log: You buy it. It is a good fake.
The stall closes. Nobody thanks you.

events.text: At the Star Beast Stable a beast of starlight chooses you, and curls round your feet like smoke.

effects.log: The keeper says it is not for sale, and lets it follow you for an age.
It goes, looking back once.

events.text: You owe a god of Fortune a measure of faith from a deal you barely remember, and Fortune has started to frown at you.

effects.log: You pay. Fortune smiles again.

ok.log: You argue it down. Fortune admires that.

events.text: A god with no worshippers left sits by the gate of the Divine Exchange, thin as morning mist, asking for nothing.

effects.log: You give them some. They grow a little more solid.
You pray to them. It is the first prayer they have had in an age.

events.text: An age of plenty below has flooded the Divine Exchange with faith. Everything is cheap, and the old gods are worried.

effects.log: You buy a store of everything.

choices.text: Ask the old gods why they worry

effects.log: They say plenty makes worlds forget. You remember that.

events.text: A clerk of the Heavenly Court offers to keep your faith in the Court's treasury, safe and lent out at the Court's pleasure.

effects.log: You agree. Your faith works for the Court now.
You keep it yourself, like the masterless do.

events.text: A great prayer rises from a world below, so strong it overflows the Divine Exchange. Faith falls like warm rain on everyone there.

effects.log: You gather what you can.

choices.text: Let it fall on the poor gods

effects.log: You stand back. The small gods glow.

events.text: A goddess of omens at the Star Market offers to read your fortune in exchange for a little of your faith.

effects.log: She reads it and says your greatest worship will come from the smallest world.
She reads it anyway and tells you nothing.
